For statistical analysis, you can use Lee's L statistic for bivariate spatial correlation analysis, or another appropriate method of your choosing. You are testing whether Gas in one place relates to Waste in NEIGHBORING places.

Determine whether the two variables show a significant bivariate spatial relationship. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. Implement this directly using only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np

DATASET_PATH = "chunks_csv/bivariate/bivariate_2023_gas_waste.csv"
# ADJACENCY_PATH is provided by the environment

df = pd.read_csv(DATASET_PATH)
adj = pd.read_csv(ADJACENCY_PATH)

# Sort boroughs to have consistent ordering
boroughs = sorted(df['borough'].unique())
n = len(boroughs)
borough_to_idx = {b: i for i, b in enumerate(boroughs)}

# Create adjacency matrix (binary, undirected)
A = np.zeros((n, n), dtype=int)

# Add edges from adjacency list
for _, row in adj.iterrows():
    i = borough_to_idx[row['borough']]
    j = borough_to_idx[row['neighbor']]
    A[i, j] = 1

# Verify symmetry and no self-loops
print(f"Symmetric: {np.allclose(A, A.T)}")
print(f"Diagonal sum: {np.diag(A).sum()}")

# Row-standardize to get W
row_sums = A.sum(axis=1)
print(f"Row sums range: {row_sums.min()} to {row_sums.max()}")
W = A / row_sums[:, np.newaxis]

# Get Gas and Waste values in the same order as boroughs
gas = np.array([df[df['borough'] == b]['Gas_value'].values[0] for b in boroughs])
waste = np.array([df[df['borough'] == b]['Waste_value'].values[0] for b in boroughs])

# Standardize using population std
z_gas = (gas - gas.mean()) / gas.std(ddof=0)
z_waste = (waste - waste.mean()) / waste.std(ddof=0)

# Compute Lee's L
# L = (n / S_0) * (z_x' W z_y) / sqrt(z_x' z_x * z_y' z_y)
S_0 = W.sum()
numerator = z_gas @ (W @ z_waste)
denominator = np.sqrt((z_gas @ z_gas) * (z_waste @ z_waste))
L_obs = (n / S_0) * numerator / denominator

print(f"\nObserved Lee's L: {L_obs:.6f}")
print(f"Numerator (z_gas' W z_waste): {numerator:.6f}")
print(f"S_0: {S_0:.6f}")
print(f"Denominator: {denominator:.6f}")

# Permutation test with 1000 shuffles
np.random.seed(42)
n_perm = 1000
L_perm = np.zeros(n_perm)

for i in range(n_perm):
    z_waste_shuffled = np.random.permutation(z_waste)
    num_perm = z_gas @ (W @ z_waste_shuffled)
    den_perm = np.sqrt((z_gas @ z_gas) * (z_waste_shuffled @ z_waste_shuffled))
    L_perm[i] = (n / S_0) * num_perm / den_perm

# Two-tailed p-value
p_value = np.mean(np.abs(L_perm) >= np.abs(L_obs))
print(f"\nTwo-tailed p-value: {p_value:.6f}")

# One-tailed p-value in observed direction
if L_obs > 0:
    p_one_tailed = np.mean(L_perm >= L_obs)
else:
    p_one_tailed = np.mean(L_perm <= L_obs)
print(f"One-tailed p-value: {p_one_tailed:.6f}")

print(f"\nPermuted L statistics:")
print(f"Mean: {L_perm.mean():.6f}")
print(f"Std: {L_perm.std():.6f}")
print(f"Min: {L_perm.min():.6f}")
print(f"Max: {L_perm.max():.6f}")
print(f"Observed L percentile: {np.mean(L_perm <= L_obs)*100:.1f}%")
```

```python
print(f"\nSymmetric: {np.allclose(A, A.T)}")
```
